_help: Weekly Pearl newsletter queue (HQ D-90, 12 Oct 2026; automatic since 3 Nov 2026). One issue a week, Tuesday 7:30am UK time, in this order. The build (lib/pearl-issue.js) writes every entry to /email/pearl/<slug>/ and /email/pearl/queue.json, and the Worker (worker/newsletter.js) sends the first ready entry that D1 newsletter_sends does not show as sent, retrying hourly that Tuesday. A missed or failed issue goes first the next Tuesday, then the queue carries on in order. 'send' is the planned date only. Add hold: true to keep an entry back. Add new entries at the end, except each month's newest Pearl, which moves near the front; rewrite the later 'send' dates a week apart, because the email's month label comes from them. The order mixes systems so consecutive issues differ.

issues.subject: Tamponade: time the collapse
issues.preheader: A wall moving inward is not the sign. The phase is. Try the question.
issues.intro: A pericardial effusion raises the question of tamponade, but its size does not answer it. This week's pearl shows the timing which does: right atrium in systole, right ventricle in early diastole.
issues.pearl: Name the phase, not just the movement: right atrium in systole, right ventricle in early diastole.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: tamponade. Right atrial collapse in systole and right ventricular collapse in early diastole.

issues.subject: Fracture ultrasound: follow the cortex
issues.preheader: The break is in the bright line at the top. Try the question.
issues.intro: Ultrasound cannot see through bone, but it shows the surface very well. This week's pearl traces the cortex and confirms a break in a second plane.
issues.pearl: Follow the cortex, not the shadow. The break is in the bright line at the top.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: fracture ultrasound. A cortical step in long axis and the same step in transverse.

issues.subject: B-lines: map the pattern
issues.preheader: B-lines are not a diagnosis. The pattern is the clue. Try the question.
issues.intro: B-lines tell you the lung has lost some air, not why. This week's pearl maps them: focal, patchy or diffuse, with a smooth or irregular pleura.
issues.pearl: Map the pattern before you name the disease: focal, patchy or diffuse, smooth or irregular pleura.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: B-lines. Focal, diffuse and aerated lung patterns.

issues.subject: Pneumoperitoneum: inspect the stripe
issues.preheader: Free air touches the peritoneum. Bowel gas sits deeper. Try the question.
issues.intro: Bowel always contains gas, so seeing gas is not enough. This week's pearl shows where free air sits, and the bright stripe it leaves behind.
issues.pearl: Decide where the gas is. Free air touches and brightens the stripe. Bowel gas sits deeper.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: pneumoperitoneum. A bright peritoneal stripe with reverberation over the liver.

issues.subject: Colour aliasing: change the scale first
issues.preheader: Red and blue mixing may just be the machine. Try the question.
issues.intro: Red and blue flickering inside a vessel can be a fast jet, or a colour scale set too low. This week's pearl sets the machine up before you interpret.
issues.pearl: Change the machine before you change the diagnosis.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: colour aliasing. Normal flow wrapping at a low scale, and smooth flow after raising it.

issues.subject: Elbow effusion: lift the fat pad
issues.preheader: If the fat pad lifts, believe the effusion. Try the question.
issues.intro: A raised posterior fat pad is the classic clue to a hidden elbow fracture. This week's pearl shows the same sign on ultrasound, and what it cannot show.
issues.pearl: If the posterior fat pad lifts, believe the effusion.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: elbow effusion. Fluid in the posterior recess lifting the posterior fat pad.

issues.subject: Cricothyroid membrane: find it before the emergency
issues.preheader: Ultrasound belongs before the emergency. Try the question.
issues.intro: In an obese or distorted neck, palpation often misses the cricothyroid membrane. This week's pearl finds and marks it while the patient is still oxygenating.
issues.pearl: Ultrasound belongs before the emergency, not between failed oxygenation and rescue.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: cricothyroid membrane. Thyroid cartilage, cricoid cartilage and the membrane between them.

issues.subject: Renal stone twinkle: a clue, not a diagnosis
issues.preheader: Twinkle should make you look harder, not stop looking. Try the question.
issues.intro: A flickering colour tail can point to a kidney stone, but many twinkling spots are not stones. This week's pearl shows the combination that is convincing.
issues.pearl: Twinkle should make you look harder on greyscale, not stop looking.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: renal stone twinkle. A stone with a twinkle tail, a shadow and hydronephrosis.

issues.subject: Tennis leg: look between the muscles
issues.preheader: A calf tear that looks like a DVT. Try the question.
issues.intro: A sudden pop in the calf during sport is often a tear of the medial gastrocnemius. This week's pearl finds it, and reminds you a DVT can coexist.
issues.pearl: The fluid collects in the plane. Look between the muscles, not just inside them.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: tennis leg. Fluid tracking between medial gastrocnemius and soleus.

issues.subject: Bowel ischaemia: read the wall
issues.preheader: Pain out of proportion. Try the question.
issues.intro: Severe pain with a soft abdomen is easy to underestimate. This week's pearl reads the bowel wall, and knows why a normal scan does not clear it.
issues.pearl: Pain out of proportion: think of the gut, then image it.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: bowel ischaemia. A thin normal bowel wall beside a thick wall without flow and with free fluid.

issues.subject: Blocked catheter: find the balloon
issues.preheader: Do not flush blind. Try the question.
issues.intro: A catheter that stops draining is blocked, misplaced or has nothing to drain. This week's pearl finds the balloon and tells you which.
issues.pearl: Do not flush blind. Find the balloon.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: blocked catheter. A balloon in an empty bladder beside a full bladder around the balloon, with clot.

issues.subject: LVOT VTI: trend the same window
issues.preheader: If the gate moved, the comparison changed. Try the question.
issues.intro: LVOT VTI tracks stroke volume, but only when you measure it the same way each time. This week's pearl shows how to make the trend believable.
issues.pearl: Repeatability is the measurement. If the gate moved, the comparison changed.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: LVOT VTI. The gate below the aortic valve, a traced envelope and a before and after trend.

issues.subject: Olecranon bursa: keep the fluid in the right layer
issues.preheader: First find the layer. Then name the fluid. Try the question.
issues.intro: A swollen point of the elbow could be a bursitis, cellulitis, an abscess or a joint effusion. This week's pearl finds the layer first.
issues.pearl: First find the layer. Then name the fluid.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: olecranon bursa. Simple and complex bursitis above the triceps tendon.

issues.subject: Groin lump: inguinal or femoral?
issues.preheader: The ligament and the vein tell you which. Try the question.
issues.intro: A groin lump may be a hernia, a node, a vein or an artery. This week's pearl finds the ligament, then the vein, and sorts them.
issues.pearl: Ligament first. Then find the vein.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: groin lump. Hernia contents in the inguinal canal beside a sac medial to the femoral vein.

issues.subject: eFAST pelvis: sweep behind the bladder
issues.preheader: The bladder is the window, not the target. Try the question.
issues.intro: Free fluid in the pelvis does not promise to sit in the middle of one image. This week's pearl sweeps behind the bladder in two planes.
issues.pearl: The bladder opens the window. The diagnosis is in the spaces behind and beside it.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: eFAST pelvis. Free fluid behind the bladder in sagittal and transverse sweeps.

issues.subject: Patellar tendon rupture: follow it to the bone
issues.preheader: The gap is the clue, not a blurred patch. Try the question.
issues.intro: Swelling can hide a patellar tendon rupture from your fingers, but not from the probe. This week's pearl follows the tendon all the way to the tibial tubercle.
issues.pearl: Follow the tendon all the way to bone. The gap is the clue, not a blurred patch.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: patellar tendon rupture. A gap with retracted tendon ends between patella and tibial tubercle.

issues.subject: Mirror artefact: read the diaphragm
issues.preheader: The mirror is normal. Losing it is the clue. Try the question.
issues.intro: A copy of the liver above the diaphragm is an artefact, and a reassuring one. This week's pearl shows why, and what it means when the copy disappears.
issues.pearl: The mirror is normal. Losing it is the clue.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: mirror artefact. The liver copied above a bright diaphragm.

issues.subject: Ankle effusion: open the anterior recess
issues.preheader: Find the talus, then look deep. Try the question.
issues.intro: A hot, swollen ankle needs one question answered first: is there fluid in the joint? This week's pearl opens the anterior recess.
issues.pearl: Find the talus, then look deep. The joint is under the tendons.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: ankle effusion. Fluid in the anterior recess between tibia and talus.

issues.subject: Liver air: portal venous gas or pneumobilia?
issues.preheader: Peripheral is portal. Central is biliary. Try the question.
issues.intro: Bright gas echoes in the liver sit in one of two places, and the difference can matter a great deal. This week's pearl shows where each kind goes, and why.
issues.pearl: Peripheral is portal. Central is biliary.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: liver air. Portal venous gas at the edge of the liver and pneumobilia near the hilum.

issues.subject: Cauda equina: measure the residual
issues.preheader: Scan after the patient tries to void. Try the question.
issues.intro: Back pain with new bladder symptoms raises a question the examination struggles to answer. This week's pearl adds one number you can measure: the post-void residual, and its limits.
issues.pearl: Measure after the patient tries to void. A normal residual does not exclude cauda equina syndrome.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: cauda equina. The bladder measured in three planes after voiding.

issues.subject: IVC clot: not every big IVC is congestion
issues.preheader: Look inside the vein before you read its size. Try the question.
issues.intro: A wide, still IVC is usually read as high right-sided pressure. This week's pearl looks inside the vein first, because clot makes it wide too.
issues.pearl: Big does not equal benign. Look inside the vein before you read its size.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: IVC clot. Echogenic thrombus within a wide IVC, extending towards the right atrium.

issues.subject: Achilles lump: xanthoma or tear?
issues.preheader: Continuity matters more than thickness. Try the question.
issues.intro: Not every thick Achilles is torn. This week's pearl separates a xanthoma, a clue to inherited high cholesterol, from a tear.
issues.pearl: Continuity matters more than thickness.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: Achilles lump. A thick but continuous tendon beside a tear with a gap.

issues.subject: Pyelonephritis: a normal scan can be normal
issues.preheader: Scan for complications, not the diagnosis. Try the question.
issues.intro: Most kidneys with pyelonephritis look normal on ultrasound. This week's pearl shows what the scan is for: the complications which change management.
issues.pearl: Use ultrasound to look for complications, not to make the diagnosis.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: pyelonephritis. A normal kidney, hydronephrosis, an abscess and the bladder.

issues.subject: Pyloric stenosis: measure, then watch
issues.preheader: Numbers matter, but passage matters too. Try the question.
issues.intro: A young baby with forceful vomiting. This week's pearl measures the pyloric muscle and channel, then watches whether anything gets through.
issues.pearl: Measure it, then watch it open.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: pyloric stenosis. The target sign in short axis and the long pyloric channel.

issues.subject: Appendix testis torsion: find the tender nub
issues.preheader: A tender nub can mimic torsion. The cord settles it. Try the question.
issues.intro: A painful scrotum in a boy is not always testicular torsion. This week's pearl finds the tiny mimic at the upper pole, and keeps the cord in view.
issues.pearl: A tender nub can mimic torsion. The cord settles the argument.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: appendix testis torsion. A small avascular nodule at the upper pole beside a testis with normal flow.

issues.subject: Neck lump: hilum or pus?
issues.preheader: Find the hilum before you call it pus. Try the question.
issues.intro: A tender neck lump is usually a node, sometimes a collection, and occasionally something more serious. This week's pearl separates them with one bright clue.
issues.pearl: Find the hilum before you call it pus.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: neck lump. An oval node with a bright hilum beside an abscess with no hilum.

issues.subject: Paracentesis: pick the pocket
issues.preheader: Not just the first black space. Try the question.
issues.intro: Most paracentesis complications come from the needle path. This week's pearl chooses the pocket and checks the route for bowel and vessels.
issues.pearl: Pick the pocket, not just the first black space.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: paracentesis. A deep fluid pocket with a clear needle path away from bowel.

issues.subject: Retained products: thick and vascular
issues.preheader: Colour separates tissue from clot. Try the question.
issues.intro: Bleeding after a pregnancy has ended. This week's pearl looks inside the uterine cavity, and uses colour Doppler to separate retained tissue from clot.
issues.pearl: Thick and vascular raises the concern. Clot is usually avascular.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: retained products. Avascular clot beside a thick endometrium with internal flow.

issues.subject: Diverticulitis: find the inflamed pouch
issues.preheader: Find the pouch. Then look at the fat. Try the question.
issues.intro: Left iliac fossa pain and fever. This week's pearl puts the probe on the point of tenderness and finds the inflamed pouch and the fat around it.
issues.pearl: Find the pouch. Then look at the fat.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: diverticulitis. An inflamed diverticulum with a thick colon wall and bright inflamed fat.

issues.subject: Scrotal fluid: clear or complex?
issues.preheader: The fluid is a window. Look at the testis. Try the question.
issues.intro: Fluid around the testis is common. This week's pearl reads the fluid, then uses it as a window onto the testis inside.
issues.pearl: Clear fluid is one story. Complex fluid is another. The testis inside tells the rest.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: scrotal fluid. A simple hydrocele beside complex fluid with septations.

issues.subject: Suprapubic catheter: fill first, then find the window
issues.preheader: A full bladder makes the safe path. Try the question.
issues.intro: When a urethral catheter will not pass, the suprapubic route needs a clear window. This week's pearl fills the bladder first and checks for bowel.
issues.pearl: Fill first, then find the window.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: suprapubic catheter. A full bladder under the abdominal wall with no bowel in the path.

issues.subject: Ascites: simple or complex?
issues.preheader: Black is simple. Debris changes the story. Try the question.
issues.intro: Ultrasound finds ascites easily. This week's pearl reads what the fluid looks like, and why a black pocket still needs a tap.
issues.pearl: Black is simple. Debris changes the story.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: ascites. Simple anechoic fluid beside complex and loculated fluid.

issues.subject: Wrist effusion: find the dorsal recess
issues.preheader: Find the recess before you chase the swelling. Try the question.
issues.intro: A hot, swollen wrist could be fluid in the joint, a tendon sheath or a cyst. This week's pearl finds the dorsal recess first.
issues.pearl: Find the dorsal recess before you chase the swelling.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: wrist effusion. Joint fluid lifting the dorsal recess over the carpal bones.

issues.subject: Optic nerve sheath: measure 3 mm behind the globe
issues.preheader: A clue to raised pressure, not a diagnosis. Try the question.
issues.intro: Raised intracranial pressure distends the sheath around the optic nerve. This week's pearl measures it properly, and says what a number can and cannot tell you.
issues.pearl: Measure 3 mm behind the globe, in two planes, in both eyes.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: optic nerve sheath. The sheath measured 3 mm behind the globe.

issues.subject: Rib fracture: trace the cortex
issues.preheader: Trace the bright line. Find the step. Try the question.
issues.intro: X-rays miss many rib fractures. This week's pearl traces the cortex where it hurts, then looks underneath for what matters more.
issues.pearl: Trace the bright line. Find the step. Then check the pleura.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: rib fracture. A step in the rib cortex with a haematoma over it.

issues.subject: Adnexal ring: not always the ectopic
issues.preheader: First find the ovary. Then judge the ring. Try the question.
issues.intro: A ring beside the uterus in early pregnancy is usually a corpus luteum, sometimes an ectopic. This week's pearl uses position to tell them apart.
issues.pearl: First find the ovary. Then judge the ring.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: adnexal ring. A corpus luteum inside the ovary beside a separate tubal ring.

issues.subject: Heel pain: thick or torn?
issues.preheader: Thickness suggests fasciitis. A gap suggests rupture. Try the question.
issues.intro: Most heel pain is plantar fasciitis, but not all. This week's pearl measures the fascia and looks for a gap.
issues.pearl: Thickness suggests fasciitis. A gap suggests rupture.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: heel pain. A thickened plantar fascia beside a fascial rupture with a gap.

issues.subject: Pleural effusion: simple or septated?
issues.preheader: Anechoic is not the same as harmless. Try the question.
issues.intro: Once you have found a pleural effusion, look inside it. This week's pearl reads the fluid, and when septations change the plan.
issues.pearl: Anechoic is not the same as harmless. Septations change the story.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: pleural effusion. Simple anechoic fluid beside a septated effusion.

issues.subject: Clavicle: follow the bright line
issues.preheader: Follow the cortex until it stops being smooth. Try the question.
issues.intro: The clavicle lies just under the skin. This week's pearl follows its cortex from end to end, and lists the injuries that cannot wait.
issues.pearl: Follow the cortex until it stops being smooth.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: clavicle. A fracture step in the clavicle cortex.

issues.subject: Finger infection: fluid in the sheath
issues.preheader: Follow the tendon. Look for fluid around it. Try the question.
issues.intro: A red, swollen finger can hide a hand surgery emergency. This week's pearl follows the flexor tendon and looks inside its sheath.
issues.pearl: Follow the tendon. Look for fluid around it.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: finger infection. Fluid around the flexor tendon inside a distended sheath.

issues.subject: Two planes: long and short or it did not happen
issues.preheader: If it matters, prove it in two planes. Try the question.
issues.intro: One slice can fool you. This week's pearl turns the probe 90 degrees and shows how a real finding holds up in both views.
issues.pearl: If it matters, prove it in two planes.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: two planes. A fluid collection in long and short axis.

issues.subject: Varicocele: veins that wake up with Valsalva
issues.preheader: Make it strain, then make the call. Try the question.
issues.intro: A bag of worms above the testis is usually a varicocele. This week's pearl uses Valsalva to confirm it, and names the ones that need a look further up.
issues.pearl: Make it strain, then make the call.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: varicocele. Dilated cord veins enlarging with colour flow during Valsalva.

issues.subject: Sweep, fan, slide: do not trust the still image
issues.preheader: The saved frame is the end of the scan. Try the question.
issues.intro: Pathology often sits a few millimetres from the frame you froze. This week's pearl moves the probe through the whole target first.
issues.pearl: A single saved frame is the end of the scan, not the scan itself.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: sweep, fan, slide. A collection missed on one frame and found after sweeping.

issues.subject: Epiglottis: find the swollen leaf
issues.preheader: Airway first. Then, if safe, find the leaf. Try the question.
issues.intro: Adult epiglottitis can hide behind a normal-looking throat. This week's pearl finds the epiglottis on the front of the neck, and says when not to scan.
issues.pearl: Find the leaf above the thyroid cartilage, then judge its shape. Never delay the airway.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: epiglottis. A thin normal epiglottis beside a thickened one in epiglottitis.

issues.subject: Distal triceps: find the olecranon attachment
issues.preheader: Follow the fibres right to the bone. Try the question.
issues.intro: Weak elbow extension after a fall is easy to miss. This week's pearl follows the triceps tendon to the olecranon, and finds the tiny flake that gives it away.
issues.pearl: Follow the fibres right to the bone.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: distal triceps. The tendon inserting on the olecranon beside a rupture with a gap.

issues.subject: Scrotal trauma: follow the tunica
issues.preheader: The outline matters more than the bruise. Try the question.
issues.intro: After a blow to the scrotum, the question is rupture. This week's pearl follows the bright tunica all the way round the testis.
issues.pearl: Follow the bright tunica, not just the bruising.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: scrotal trauma. A testis with an intact tunica beside a ruptured testis with a broken outline.

issues.subject: Pectoralis major tear: look beyond the shoulder
issues.preheader: An absent tendon at the humerus is the clue. Try the question.
issues.intro: A pop during a bench press is often called a shoulder sprain. This week's pearl follows the pectoralis tendon to the humerus.
issues.pearl: An absent tendon at the humerus is the clue.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: pectoralis major. The normal tendon at the humerus beside a retracted complete tear.

issues.subject: Partial testicular torsion: flow does not clear it
issues.preheader: Flow present is not torsion excluded. Try the question.
issues.intro: A partly twisted cord can still show colour flow. This week's pearl compares both sides and reads the arterial waveform, and keeps urology first.
issues.pearl: Flow present is not torsion excluded.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: partial torsion. Persisting colour flow with a high-resistance arterial waveform.

issues.subject: NG tube: ultrasound is a scout, not clearance
issues.preheader: A clue is not confirmation. Try the question.
issues.intro: Ultrasound can show a nasogastric tube in the neck. This week's pearl shows where to look, and why pH or X-ray still decides.
issues.pearl: A sonographic clue is not permission to use the tube.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: NG tube. The left neck with trachea, thyroid, carotid and the tube in the oesophagus.

issues.subject: Eye trauma: has the lens moved?
issues.preheader: Find the lens first. Try the question.
issues.intro: After a blow to the eye, the lens can fall back into the vitreous. This week's pearl finds it through the closed lid, gently.
issues.pearl: Look for the lens, without pressing on the globe.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: lens dislocation. The lens behind the iris, and a dislocated lens on the posterior wall.

issues.subject: Pyomyositis: look below the fascia
issues.preheader: Deep pain, deep scan. Try the question.
issues.intro: Deep muscle pain with fever is easy to call a strain. This week's pearl scans past the fat into the muscle.
issues.pearl: If the pain is deep, scan beyond the subcutaneous fat.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: pyomyositis. Striated muscle under the fascia and a deep pocket inside it.

issues.subject: Sternoclavicular joint: look for capsular lift
issues.preheader: Compare both sides. Try the question.
issues.intro: A hot sternoclavicular joint is rare and easily missed. This week's pearl looks for fluid lifting the capsule.
issues.pearl: Scan the small joint. Think about the deep structures.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: sternoclavicular joint. The normal joint and an effusion lifting the capsule.

issues.subject: Dental swelling: find the vestibular pocket
issues.preheader: Pocket or cellulitis? Try the question.
issues.intro: Facial swelling from a tooth can be pus or cellulitis. This week's pearl finds the pocket beside the jaw, and checks the airway first.
issues.pearl: Find the pocket. Check the airway and the source.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: dental swelling. Oedema over the jaw, and a pocket beside the bone with flow in its rim.

issues.subject: Thoracentesis: mark the pocket
issues.preheader: See the diaphragm first. Try the question.
issues.intro: A blunted angle on the X-ray is not a needle site. This week's pearl finds the pocket that stays clear of lung and diaphragm through every breath.
issues.pearl: See the diaphragm. See the fluid. Then choose the site.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: thoracentesis. A pleural pocket above the diaphragm, the depth from skin to fluid, and a needle path above the rib.

issues.subject: Carotid dissection: look for the intimal flap
issues.preheader: A flap is a clue, not clearance. Try the question.
issues.intro: Neck pain with a small pupil in a younger patient can be a carotid dissection. This week's pearl looks for the flap, and keeps the stroke pathway first.
issues.pearl: If you see a flap, think dissection.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: carotid dissection. A normal carotid beside an intimal flap with true and false lumens.

issues.subject: Parotid swelling: find the collection
issues.preheader: Parotitis or pus? Try the question.
issues.intro: A hot swelling in front of the ear is usually parotitis. This week's pearl finds the few that hold a pocket, and remembers the facial nerve.
issues.pearl: Find the pocket. Then assess the depth and extent.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: parotid swelling. Diffuse parotitis beside a parotid abscess with flow in its rim.

issues.subject: Penile fracture: find the tunica break
issues.preheader: Follow the bright capsule. Try the question.
issues.intro: A snap, a lost erection and rapid swelling. This week's pearl follows the tunica albuginea, and keeps urology first.
issues.pearl: Find the capsule. Do not let the scan delay referral.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: penile fracture. A continuous tunica beside a tunica break with haematoma at the defect.

issues.subject: Retropharyngeal abscess: look behind the pharynx
issues.preheader: Airway first, then the picture. Try the question.
issues.intro: A feverish child who will not extend the neck. This week's pearl looks behind the pharynx, and knows when not to scan.
issues.pearl: If the airway is threatened, treat the patient before the picture.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: retropharyngeal abscess. The probe on the lateral neck and a collection behind the pharynx.

issues.subject: Priapism: read the cavernosal flow
issues.preheader: Low flow is time-critical. Try the question.
issues.intro: A painful erection over four hours is an emergency. This week's pearl reads the cavernosal flow, and never lets the scan delay aspiration.
issues.pearl: Low flow is time-critical. Do not wait for a perfect scan.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: priapism. No cavernosal flow in ischaemic priapism beside a focal high-flow blush.

issues.subject: Abscess drainage: plan the needle path
issues.preheader: Colour first. Try the question.
issues.intro: Before anyone picks up a blade, a minute with the probe gives the depth, the vessels and the route. This week's pearl plans the needle path.
issues.pearl: Colour first. Then choose the path.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: abscess drainage. Calipers across a dark pocket, and colour flow in its rim with an artery beside it.

issues.subject: Strangulated hernia: read the sac
issues.preheader: Stuck is one thing. Dying bowel is another. Try the question.
issues.intro: A hernia that will not go back may be stuck, or it may be dying. This week's pearl reads the sac, and knows when the scan cannot reassure you.
issues.pearl: If it hurts and will not go back, call the surgeons.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: strangulated hernia. A thin-walled loop through a fascial defect beside a thick-walled loop with fluid in the sac.

issues.subject: Liver abscess: fever and a dark round pocket
issues.preheader: When the gallbladder does not explain the fever. Try the question.
issues.intro: Fever and right upper quadrant pain, and a gallbladder that looks fine. This week's pearl sweeps the rest of the liver.
issues.pearl: Fever and right upper quadrant pain: sweep the whole liver.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: liver abscess. Normal even liver beside a round dark lesion with debris and bright tissue behind it.

issues.subject: Stone at the bladder: look behind it
issues.preheader: A full bladder is a window. Try the question.
issues.intro: Most of the ureter hides behind bowel gas, but its lowest part sits right behind the bladder. This week's pearl looks there.
issues.pearl: Fill the bladder. Then look behind it.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: stone at the bladder. A smooth bladder back wall with a ureteric jet, beside a bright echo with a shadow.

issues.subject: Breast abscess: aspirate before you cut
issues.preheader: Mastitis or a collection? Try the question.
issues.intro: A hot, tender breast may be mastitis or an abscess, and the treatment differs. This week's pearl finds the pocket.
issues.pearl: Find the pocket. Needle first, blade later.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: breast abscess. Bright swollen tissue with no pocket, beside an irregular dark pocket with debris.

issues.subject: Perianal abscess: judge the depth
issues.preheader: A small lump can have a deep root. Try the question.
issues.intro: The lump on the skin says little about what lies beneath it. This week's pearl judges the depth, and knows what ultrasound can miss.
issues.pearl: A small lump can have a deep root.
issues.alt: Wavelength Pearl: perianal abscess. A shallow dark pocket under the skin, beside a deep collection tracking towards the sphincter.
